cluster_name: Burnham Kyiv visit: UK releases SCALP missile blueprints to Ukraine
tldr: Headline coverage splits into two near-equal clusters: a missile-transfer narrative (UK sharing SCALP/Storm Shadow blueprints so Ukraine can build long-range missiles locally) and a diplomatic-lobbying narrative (Burnham planning a September US trip to press Trump for Patriot interceptors). Russian-state and Kremlin-proximate headlines occupy a distinct third register, framing the UK as an active conflict participant and threatening production sites — a counter-framing invisible in the remaining nine-outlet consensus. Germany and The Independent alone surface a moral-historical layer, foregrounding WWII analogy and direct Putin challenge at headline level.
event_summary: UK PM Andy Burnham visited Kyiv on 24 August for Ukraine's Independence Day, announcing that defence firm MBDA would release classified SCALP missile component data to enable local production in Ukraine; he also signalled plans to lobby Trump in September for Patriot air-defence interceptors.

silences.what_they_covered_instead: The Inquirer's headline ('New UK PM Andy Burnham to make visit to Kyiv on Monday – office') is a bare logistical announcement — new PM, destination, timing — carrying no security, political, or moral framing detectable at homepage level; a reader sees only that a visit is scheduled.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to assert that Britain is 'participating in and intensifying' the conflict — sole outlet to advertise the Kremlin co-belligerent framing at the homepage level, positioning the UK as a war party rather than a supporter.

Only headline in the corpus to foreground Burnham's WWII moral analogy ('likens Ukraine fight to British stand against Nazis'), surfacing a historical-ethical register entirely absent from all other outlet titles.

Only headline to cast Burnham's language as a direct personal challenge to Putin ('Who started the fire?'), the most confrontational register in the corpus — uniquely personalised and adversarial at headline level.

Only headline to embed both the UK announcement and Moscow's immediate counter-move in a single sentence, making the rapid-response timeline ('Hours later, the Kremlin announced…Russian forces are already working to find the production sites') the primary advertised information unit.

bottom_line: At the headline layer the story is two announcements — UK sharing missile blueprints (SECURITY_DEFENSE) and Burnham en route to lobby Trump for Patriot interceptors (POLITICAL) — while Russian-proximate and Kremlin-facing headlines uniquely advertise the UK as an active conflict participant, a counter-framing suppressed across the remaining nine-outlet consensus.
